title: Functional API with a cache: a running task can match the cache, so its writes change under it (`IndexError: deque index out of range`)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangGraph rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Related Issues / PRs

- #9304: `dictionary changed size during iteration` in the same code, from a different race. This one remains once that one is fixed, see below.


### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import collections
import sys
from importlib.metadata import version

from langgraph.cache.memory import InMemoryCache
from langgraph.func import entrypoint, task
from langgraph.types import CachePolicy

sys.setswitchinterval(5e-6)  # Makes the failure frequent enough to see on any machine.


@task(cache_policy=CachePolicy())
def leaf(i):
    return i


@task(cache_policy=CachePolicy())
def parent(i):
    return [future.result() for future in [leaf(j) for j in range(8)]]


def run():
    @entrypoint(cache=InMemoryCache())  # A cache of its own, so that it starts empty.
    def workflow(n):
        return [future.result() for future in [parent(i) for i in range(4)]]

    for _ in workflow.stream(1):
        pass


outcomes = collections.Counter()
for _ in range(300):
    try:
        run()
        outcomes["ok"] += 1
    except Exception as error:
        outcomes[f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:60]}"] += 1
print("langgraph", version("langgraph"))
for outcome, count in outcomes.most_common():
    print(count, outcome)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
langgraph 1.2.19
170 RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration
61 RuntimeError: deque mutated during iteration
55 ok
14 IndexError: deque index out of range

  File ".../langgraph/pregel/_loop.py", line 1749, in accept_push
    self.put_writes(task.id, task.writes, cached=True)
  File ".../langgraph/pregel/_loop.py", line 1793, in put_writes
    super().put_writes(task_id, writes, cached=cached)
  File ".../langgraph/pregel/_loop.py", line 557, in put_writes
    self.output_writes(task_id, writes, cached=cached)
  File ".../langgraph/pregel/_loop.py", line 1607, in output_writes
    if writes[0][0] == INTERRUPT:
       ~~~~~~^^^
IndexError: deque index out of range
```

### Description

A functional workflow that runs cached tasks concurrently crashes under the sync API. Every task succeeds, but the run aborts with `RuntimeError: deque mutated during iteration` or `IndexError: deque index out of range`, raised from LangGraph's own bookkeeping, so the application loses the whole run and can do nothing about it.

It happens without any special setup: with the `setswitchinterval` line removed and a 1 ms `time.sleep` in `leaf`, standing for a call to a service, 9 of 300 runs fail with these errors on Ubuntu.

`SyncPregelLoop.accept_push` calls `match_cached_writes` each time a task is pushed, and that method looks at every task in `self.tasks` with a cache key and no writes:

```python
cached = {(t.cache_key.ns, t.cache_key.key): t for t in self.tasks.values() if t.cache_key and not t.writes}
```

A task that is already running also has no writes yet. So when a sibling pushes a task, a running task can match the cache. Its `task.writes` deque is then extended and passed to `put_writes`, which iterates it, while the thread running the task can clear it (`task.writes.clear()` at the start of an attempt in `run_with_retry`) or write to it. That is the mutation in the errors above.

Fixing #9304 does not fix this. With a lock around task registration and cache matching (the change of PR #9515), `dictionary changed size` goes away and these errors stay:

```text
295 ok
2 IndexError: deque index out of range
2 RuntimeError: deque mutated during iteration
1 IndexError: list index out of range
```

Looking up only the task just pushed fixes it. With that lock and this change, all 300 runs are `ok`, and so are all 600 runs of a larger test in which the lock alone failed 27 times:

```python
if pushed := super().accept_push(task, write_idx, call):
    if pushed.cache_key and not pushed.writes and self.cache is not None:
        key = (pushed.cache_key.ns, pushed.cache_key.key)
        for values in self.cache.get((key,)).values():
            pushed.writes.extend(values)
            self.put_writes(pushed.id, pushed.writes, cached=True)
```


### System Info

System Information
------------------
> OS:  Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5), and Darwin
> Python Version:  3.12.13

Package Information
-------------------
> langgraph: 1.2.19
> langgraph-checkpoint: 4.3.1
> langchain_core: 1.7.3

title: asyncio.iscoroutinefunction usage in checkpoint store embed is deprecated in Python 3.14
body:
### Description

`_is_async_callable()` in `libs/checkpoint/langgraph/store/base/embed.py` uses `asyncio.iscoroutinefunction` (twice), which is deprecated as of Python 3.14. The CPython docs recommend `inspect.iscoroutinefunction` as the drop-in replacement (the two are functionally identical).

This helper is used to dispatch embed/store operations between sync and async paths, so on Python 3.14 every store operation that goes through it emits a `DeprecationWarning`.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import warnings
warnings.simplefilter("always")

from langgraph.store.base.embed import _is_async_callable

async def f(): ...

_is_async_callable(f)
# On Python 3.14 this raises:
# DeprecationWarning: 'asyncio.iscoroutinefunction' is deprecated and will be removed;
# use 'inspect.iscoroutinefunction' instead
```

(Note: identified by static inspection against the CPython 3.14 asyncio deprecations; the repro above is what a 3.14 interpreter emits per the official deprecation notice.)

### Expected behavior

No `DeprecationWarning` from LangGraph internals on Python 3.14.

### Suggested fix

Replace the two `asyncio.iscoroutinefunction` calls in `_is_async_callable()` with `inspect.iscoroutinefunction` (and the `asyncio` import with `inspect`). I have a PR implementing exactly this change (currently closed by the missing-issue-link workflow); I will re-link it as `Fixes #<this issue>` per the workflow instructions.

### System Info

Any platform; Python 3.14 with the current `main` branch of `libs/checkpoint`. The affected helper is exercised by all embed-based store implementations (e.g. InMemoryStore, PostgresStore with embeddings).

title: sdk-py: a stream that drops before its first event reconnects without limit
body:
### Description

`StreamController` and `SyncStreamController` reopen the shared SSE after a transport drop, with a budget of `max_reconnect_attempts` (default 5). That budget only counts reconnects that fail to **open**: `_reconnect_shared_stream` returns `True` as soon as the new stream reaches `ready`, so a peer that accepts the connection and then ends it before sending a single event resets the budget on every cycle.

The subscription never terminates. Against a peer that keeps accepting, the client reconnects for as long as the peer allows it, and the caller sees neither events nor an error.

The client-stream path already states the intended rule — #9462 resets its five attempts "once a reconnect yields an event". The v3 controllers reset on a successful open instead, which is why the same peer behaviour is bounded there and unbounded here.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

Real socket, no mocks. The server answers the SSE POST with `200` + `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and then closes the connection mid-body without a terminating chunk — what a proxy or load balancer does when it kills a connection.

```python
import asyncio
import contextlib
import time

import httpx

from langgraph_sdk.stream.controller import StreamController
from langgraph_sdk.stream.transport.http import ProtocolSseTransport

HEADERS = (
    b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n"
    b"Content-Type: text/event-stream\r\n"
    b"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n"
    b"\r\n"
)


class DropServer:
    """Answers every request with 200 + chunked, then hangs up without sending an event."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.connections = 0

    async def handle(self, reader, writer) -> None:
        self.connections += 1
        with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
            await asyncio.wait_for(reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n"), timeout=5)
        try:
            writer.write(HEADERS)
            await writer.drain()
            writer.close()          # FIN mid-body: truncated chunked payload
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                await writer.wait_closed()
        except Exception:
            pass


async def main() -> None:
    state = DropServer()
    server = await asyncio.start_server(state.handle, "127.0.0.1", 0)
    port = server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]

    client = httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}", timeout=httpx.Timeout(30.0))
    controller = StreamController(transport=ProtocolSseTransport(client=client, thread_id="thread-1"))

    finished = False

    async def consume() -> None:
        nonlocal finished
        async for _ in controller.subscribe(["values"]):
            pass
        finished = True

    task = asyncio.create_task(consume())
    started = time.monotonic()
    await asyncio.sleep(5.0)

    print(f"connections accepted in {time.monotonic() - started:.1f}s: {state.connections}")
    print(f"subscription finished: {finished}")

    task.cancel()
    with contextlib.suppress(BaseException):
        await task
    await controller.close()
    await client.aclose()
    server.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

Output on `main` (`e5c961d7`), and with the patch below applied:

| | connections accepted in 5s | subscription finished |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | **518** | `False` |
| patched | **6** | `True` |

(The exact count is just how fast the loop spins on this machine; repeated runs on `main` landed between roughly 410 and 520. The point is that nothing bounds it.)

Two neighbouring cases, same harness, for contrast — neither reconnects on `main`, so they are not part of this report:

- a clean end (proper `0\r\n\r\n` terminator): 1 connection, the subscription finishes normally.
- an immediate TCP reset after the headers: 1 connection, no reconnect.

### Root cause

`_reconnect_shared_stream` treats *a stream that reached `ready`* as a successful attempt, and a stream that reached `ready` then dropped counts for nothing — so a drop after a successful open never advances the budget.

### Expected behavior

A reconnect that delivers no event before dropping should count against the same budget as a reconnect that fails to open, and should back off before retrying, so a peer that accepts and immediately ends connections cannot hold the client in a reconnect loop.

### Notes

When the budget is exhausted today, the subscription ends and subscriber queues receive the end-of-stream sentinel — no error reaches the caller. Whether that should raise instead is a public-API decision, so the patch below leaves it as is.

### Related Issues / PRs

- #9462 — the client-stream path that documents "reset the five attempts once a reconnect yields an event"
- #9499 — an idle stream whose read timeout is held open by heartbeat comments
- #9500 — the client timeout not applying to the in-process transport

Updates `pytest` from 9.1.1 to 9.2.0
Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

    They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see 10819 and 14011.

  • #14808: Passing a non-string value to a string-typed ini option now emits a pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning. This affects [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml. In pytest 10 this will raise a TypeError, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.

  • #7323: Passing bytes to TerminalReporter.write_line() is now deprecated, pass a str instead.

New features

  • #14743: Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output.
  • #2781: When strict_markers is enabled, marker names used in -m expressions are now validated against registered markers.
  • #6881: Added the parametrize_long_str_id_strategy configuration option to control how long str/bytes parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ids=[...] or pytest.param(..., id=...) are not affected. Available strategies: short (default, values over 100 chars fall back to argname+index), sha256 (SHA-256 hex digest), legacy (keep full value), and disallow (error requesting explicit IDs).

Improvements in existing functionality

  • #10745: A RecursionError whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass --full-trace to see every frame.

Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

    They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see 10819 and 14011.

  • #14808: Passing a non-string value to a string-typed ini option now emits a pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning. This affects [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml. In pytest 10 this will raise a TypeError, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.

  • #7323: Passing bytes to TerminalReporter.write_line() is now deprecated, pass a str instead.

New features

  • #14743: Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output.
  • #2781: When strict_markers is enabled, marker names used in -m expressions are now validated against registered markers.
  • #6881: Added the parametrize_long_str_id_strategy configuration option to control how long str/bytes parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ids=[...] or pytest.param(..., id=...) are not affected. Available strategies: short (default, values over 100 chars fall back to argname+index), sha256 (SHA-256 hex digest), legacy (keep full value), and disallow (error requesting explicit IDs).

Improvements in existing functionality

  • #10745: A RecursionError whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass --full-trace to see every frame.

Updates `pytest-mock` from 3.16.0 to 3.17.0
Release notes

Sourced from pytest-mock's releases.

v3.17.0

2026-10-17

  • #641: Failures of mock assertions such as assert_called_with are again reported only once, instead of two or three times with the original error from the mock module chained before them.
  • #642: Mock assertion failures no longer show misleading introspection when they are not about the arguments of the last call: assert_called, assert_called_once, assert_not_called, assert_any_call, their await counterparts, and assert_called_once_with/assert_awaited_once_with when the mock was not called (awaited) exactly once. The introspection also no longer reports arguments passed by position versus by keyword as different for autospecced mocks, and no longer shows empty Args:/Kwargs: sections when assertion rewriting is not available.
  • #643: assert_has_calls and assert_has_awaits failures no longer show pytest introspection, which compared the expected and actual calls position by position and so reported differences between unrelated calls. The mock's own message, listing the expected and actual calls, is still shown.

v3.16.1

2026-10-17

  • #617: Fixed assert_has_calls raising ValueError instead of AssertionError (or showing misleading introspection) when the expected calls are plain tuples rather than call(...) objects, such as (args, kwargs) entries of another mock's call_args_list, (args,), (kwargs,), (name, args) or (name, kwargs).
  • #621: Fixed mocker.stop() sometimes stopping the wrong mock, for example with mocks from mocker.create_autospec.
  • #621: mocker.stop() now undoes the most recent patch first when the same object is used in several patches.
  • #623: Fixed misleading introspection in assert_has_awaits failures, and assert_has_calls/assert_has_awaits raising IndexError instead of AssertionError when calls is passed by keyword.
  • #624: Clear spy_return_iter after a spied synchronous or asynchronous function raises, matching spy_return.
  • #627: Document async_stub await assertions and the distinction between call and await tracking.
  • #629: Fixed mocker.resetall() skipping the mocks patched with mocker.patch.multiple(), both the ones it creates and the ones passed explicitly.
  • #630: mocker.resetall() now also resets spy_return and spy_exception of spies, like it already did for spy_return_list and spy_return_iter, and no longer overwrites attributes with these names on mocks that are not spies.
  • #633: Fixed spies on classmethod, staticmethod, builtins and classes returning a MagicMock instead of calling the spied code after mocker.resetall(side_effect=True). Resetting a spy's side_effect now goes back to calling the spied code, also clearing any side_effect set on the spy.

Updates `pytest` from 9.1.1 to 9.2.0
Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

    They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see 10819 and 14011.

  • #14808: Passing a non-string value to a string-typed ini option now emits a pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning. This affects [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml. In pytest 10 this will raise a TypeError, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.

  • #7323: Passing bytes to TerminalReporter.write_line() is now deprecated, pass a str instead.

New features

  • #14743: Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output.
  • #2781: When strict_markers is enabled, marker names used in -m expressions are now validated against registered markers.
  • #6881: Added the parametrize_long_str_id_strategy configuration option to control how long str/bytes parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ids=[...] or pytest.param(..., id=...) are not affected. Available strategies: short (default, values over 100 chars fall back to argname+index), sha256 (SHA-256 hex digest), legacy (keep full value), and disallow (error requesting explicit IDs).

Improvements in existing functionality

  • #10745: A RecursionError whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass --full-trace to see every frame.

Updates `pytest-mock` from 3.16.0 to 3.17.0
Release notes

Sourced from pytest-mock's releases.

v3.17.0

2026-10-17

  • #641: Failures of mock assertions such as assert_called_with are again reported only once, instead of two or three times with the original error from the mock module chained before them.
  • #642: Mock assertion failures no longer show misleading introspection when they are not about the arguments of the last call: assert_called, assert_called_once, assert_not_called, assert_any_call, their await counterparts, and assert_called_once_with/assert_awaited_once_with when the mock was not called (awaited) exactly once. The introspection also no longer reports arguments passed by position versus by keyword as different for autospecced mocks, and no longer shows empty Args:/Kwargs: sections when assertion rewriting is not available.
  • #643: assert_has_calls and assert_has_awaits failures no longer show pytest introspection, which compared the expected and actual calls position by position and so reported differences between unrelated calls. The mock's own message, listing the expected and actual calls, is still shown.

v3.16.1

2026-10-17

  • #617: Fixed assert_has_calls raising ValueError instead of AssertionError (or showing misleading introspection) when the expected calls are plain tuples rather than call(...) objects, such as (args, kwargs) entries of another mock's call_args_list, (args,), (kwargs,), (name, args) or (name, kwargs).
  • #621: Fixed mocker.stop() sometimes stopping the wrong mock, for example with mocks from mocker.create_autospec.
  • #621: mocker.stop() now undoes the most recent patch first when the same object is used in several patches.
  • #623: Fixed misleading introspection in assert_has_awaits failures, and assert_has_calls/assert_has_awaits raising IndexError instead of AssertionError when calls is passed by keyword.
  • #624: Clear spy_return_iter after a spied synchronous or asynchronous function raises, matching spy_return.
  • #627: Document async_stub await assertions and the distinction between call and await tracking.
  • #629: Fixed mocker.resetall() skipping the mocks patched with mocker.patch.multiple(), both the ones it creates and the ones passed explicitly.
  • #630: mocker.resetall() now also resets spy_return and spy_exception of spies, like it already did for spy_return_list and spy_return_iter, and no longer overwrites attributes with these names on mocks that are not spies.
  • #633: Fixed spies on classmethod, staticmethod, builtins and classes returning a MagicMock instead of calling the spied code after mocker.resetall(side_effect=True). Resetting a spy's side_effect now goes back to calling the spied code, also clearing any side_effect set on the spy.

Updates `pytest` from 9.1.1 to 9.2.0
Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

    They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see 10819 and 14011.

  • #14808: Passing a non-string value to a string-typed ini option now emits a pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning. This affects [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml. In pytest 10 this will raise a TypeError, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.

  • #7323: Passing bytes to TerminalReporter.write_line() is now deprecated, pass a str instead.

New features

  • #14743: Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output.
  • #2781: When strict_markers is enabled, marker names used in -m expressions are now validated against registered markers.
  • #6881: Added the parametrize_long_str_id_strategy configuration option to control how long str/bytes parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ids=[...] or pytest.param(..., id=...) are not affected. Available strategies: short (default, values over 100 chars fall back to argname+index), sha256 (SHA-256 hex digest), legacy (keep full value), and disallow (error requesting explicit IDs).

Improvements in existing functionality

  • #10745: A RecursionError whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass --full-trace to see every frame.

Updates `pytest-mock` from 3.16.0 to 3.17.0
Release notes

Sourced from pytest-mock's releases.

v3.17.0

2026-10-17

  • #641: Failures of mock assertions such as assert_called_with are again reported only once, instead of two or three times with the original error from the mock module chained before them.
  • #642: Mock assertion failures no longer show misleading introspection when they are not about the arguments of the last call: assert_called, assert_called_once, assert_not_called, assert_any_call, their await counterparts, and assert_called_once_with/assert_awaited_once_with when the mock was not called (awaited) exactly once. The introspection also no longer reports arguments passed by position versus by keyword as different for autospecced mocks, and no longer shows empty Args:/Kwargs: sections when assertion rewriting is not available.
  • #643: assert_has_calls and assert_has_awaits failures no longer show pytest introspection, which compared the expected and actual calls position by position and so reported differences between unrelated calls. The mock's own message, listing the expected and actual calls, is still shown.

v3.16.1

2026-10-17

  • #617: Fixed assert_has_calls raising ValueError instead of AssertionError (or showing misleading introspection) when the expected calls are plain tuples rather than call(...) objects, such as (args, kwargs) entries of another mock's call_args_list, (args,), (kwargs,), (name, args) or (name, kwargs).
  • #621: Fixed mocker.stop() sometimes stopping the wrong mock, for example with mocks from mocker.create_autospec.
  • #621: mocker.stop() now undoes the most recent patch first when the same object is used in several patches.
  • #623: Fixed misleading introspection in assert_has_awaits failures, and assert_has_calls/assert_has_awaits raising IndexError instead of AssertionError when calls is passed by keyword.
  • #624: Clear spy_return_iter after a spied synchronous or asynchronous function raises, matching spy_return.
  • #627: Document async_stub await assertions and the distinction between call and await tracking.
  • #629: Fixed mocker.resetall() skipping the mocks patched with mocker.patch.multiple(), both the ones it creates and the ones passed explicitly.
  • #630: mocker.resetall() now also resets spy_return and spy_exception of spies, like it already did for spy_return_list and spy_return_iter, and no longer overwrites attributes with these names on mocks that are not spies.
  • #633: Fixed spies on classmethod, staticmethod, builtins and classes returning a MagicMock instead of calling the spied code after mocker.resetall(side_effect=True). Resetting a spy's side_effect now goes back to calling the spied code, also clearing any side_effect set on the spy.

Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

    They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see 10819 and 14011.

  • #14808: Passing a non-string value to a string-typed ini option now emits a pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning. This affects [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml. In pytest 10 this will raise a TypeError, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.

  • #7323: Passing bytes to TerminalReporter.write_line() is now deprecated, pass a str instead.

New features

  • #14743: Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output.
  • #2781: When strict_markers is enabled, marker names used in -m expressions are now validated against registered markers.
  • #6881: Added the parametrize_long_str_id_strategy configuration option to control how long str/bytes parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ids=[...] or pytest.param(..., id=...) are not affected. Available strategies: short (default, values over 100 chars fall back to argname+index), sha256 (SHA-256 hex digest), legacy (keep full value), and disallow (error requesting explicit IDs).

Improvements in existing functionality

  • #10745: A RecursionError whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass --full-trace to see every frame.

Updates `pytest-mock` from 3.16.0 to 3.17.0
Release notes

Sourced from pytest-mock's releases.

v3.17.0

2026-10-17

  • #641: Failures of mock assertions such as assert_called_with are again reported only once, instead of two or three times with the original error from the mock module chained before them.
  • #642: Mock assertion failures no longer show misleading introspection when they are not about the arguments of the last call: assert_called, assert_called_once, assert_not_called, assert_any_call, their await counterparts, and assert_called_once_with/assert_awaited_once_with when the mock was not called (awaited) exactly once. The introspection also no longer reports arguments passed by position versus by keyword as different for autospecced mocks, and no longer shows empty Args:/Kwargs: sections when assertion rewriting is not available.
  • #643: assert_has_calls and assert_has_awaits failures no longer show pytest introspection, which compared the expected and actual calls position by position and so reported differences between unrelated calls. The mock's own message, listing the expected and actual calls, is still shown.

v3.16.1

2026-10-17

  • #617: Fixed assert_has_calls raising ValueError instead of AssertionError (or showing misleading introspection) when the expected calls are plain tuples rather than call(...) objects, such as (args, kwargs) entries of another mock's call_args_list, (args,), (kwargs,), (name, args) or (name, kwargs).
  • #621: Fixed mocker.stop() sometimes stopping the wrong mock, for example with mocks from mocker.create_autospec.
  • #621: mocker.stop() now undoes the most recent patch first when the same object is used in several patches.
  • #623: Fixed misleading introspection in assert_has_awaits failures, and assert_has_calls/assert_has_awaits raising IndexError instead of AssertionError when calls is passed by keyword.
  • #624: Clear spy_return_iter after a spied synchronous or asynchronous function raises, matching spy_return.
  • #627: Document async_stub await assertions and the distinction between call and await tracking.
  • #629: Fixed mocker.resetall() skipping the mocks patched with mocker.patch.multiple(), both the ones it creates and the ones passed explicitly.
  • #630: mocker.resetall() now also resets spy_return and spy_exception of spies, like it already did for spy_return_list and spy_return_iter, and no longer overwrites attributes with these names on mocks that are not spies.
  • #633: Fixed spies on classmethod, staticmethod, builtins and classes returning a MagicMock instead of calling the spied code after mocker.resetall(side_effect=True). Resetting a spy's side_effect now goes back to calling the spied code, also clearing any side_effect set on the spy.

Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

v3.17.0

2026-10-17

  • #641: Failures of mock assertions such as assert_called_with are again reported only once, instead of two or three times with the original error from the mock module chained before them.

title: `AsyncBatchedBaseStore` skips the `str(key)` coercion `BaseStore` applies, so `AsyncSqliteStore.aget(ns, 42)` misses an item written with `aput(ns, 42, ...)`

### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangGraph rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import asyncio

from langgraph.store.sqlite import SqliteStore
from langgraph.store.sqlite.aio import AsyncSqliteStore


def sync() -> None:
    with SqliteStore.from_conn_string(":memory:") as store:
        store.setup()
        store.put(("users",), 42, {"v": 1})
        print("SqliteStore.get(42):", store.get(("users",), 42))


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncSqliteStore.from_conn_string(":memory:") as store:
        await store.setup()
        await store.aput(("users",), 42, {"v": 1})
        print("AsyncSqliteStore.aget(42):", await store.aget(("users",), 42))
        print("AsyncSqliteStore.aget('42'):", await store.aget(("users",), "42"))


sync()
asyncio.run(main())
```

Output:

```
SqliteStore.get(42): Item(namespace=['users'], key='42', value={'v': 1}, ...)
AsyncSqliteStore.aget(42): None
AsyncSqliteStore.aget('42'): Item(namespace=['users'], key='42', value={'v': 1}, ...)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

_No response_

### Description

`BaseStore.get/put/delete` and `aget/aput/adelete` all build their ops with `str(key)` (`libs/checkpoint/langgraph/store/base/__init__.py`). `AsyncBatchedBaseStore` (`libs/checkpoint/langgraph/store/base/batch.py`) overrides `aget`/`aput`/`adelete` to queue ops for batching, but passes `key` through unchanged. So the async stores built on it (`AsyncSqliteStore`, `AsyncPostgresStore`) don't match their sync versions or `InMemoryStore`: in the example the item is written under `'42'`, but `aget(ns, 42)` returns `None`.

Proposed fix: coerce non-str keys with `str(key)` in the `GetOp`/`PutOp` built by those three methods, like `BaseStore` does. str subclasses (e.g. `class Key(str, Enum)`) would be passed through unchanged, so keys already written through the async stores stay readable. This doesn't add a new accepted type; it makes the batched store match the base class. I have the change and a regression test ready, and would like to be assigned to open the PR.

title: `task(fn, name=...)` renames the user function in place, so named tasks sharing a function all run under the last name

### Checked other resources

- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.

- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from langgraph.func import entrypoint, task


def summarize(text: str) -> str:
    return text.upper()


summarize_a = task(summarize, name="summarize_a")
summarize_b = task(summarize, name="summarize_b")


@entrypoint()
def workflow(text: str) -> str:
    a = summarize_a(text).result()
    return summarize_b(a).result()


print(summarize.__name__)
for chunk in workflow.stream("hi", stream_mode="updates"):
    print(chunk)
```

Output:

```
summarize_b
{'summarize_b': 'HI'}
{'summarize_b': 'HI'}
{'workflow': 'HI'}
```

Expected:

```
summarize
{'summarize_a': 'HI'}
{'summarize_b': 'HI'}
{'workflow': 'HI'}
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

_No response_

### Description

When `name=` is passed, `_TaskFunction.__init__` (`libs/langgraph/langgraph/func/__init__.py`) does `func.__name__ = name` on the user's function. So when the same function is used for more than one named task, every task runs, streams and checkpoints under the last name given, and the user's function is renamed everywhere else too.

Bound methods already avoid this by wrapping in a `functools.partial` first (the comment there says it's "to avoid modifying the original class method in case it's shared across multiple tasks"). Plain functions and partials don't get the same treatment.

Proposed fix: wrap functions and partials the same way, `functools.update_wrapper(functools.partial(func), func)`, and set `__name__` on the wrapper. `update_wrapper` copies `__module__`/`__qualname__`, so `identifier()` and cache keys stay the same. Callable instances can keep the current path (wrapping them in a partial would hide an async `__call__` from `is_async_callable`). I have the change with sync/async regression tests ready, and would like to be assigned to open the PR.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

Save as a file and run (the future import has to be at the top of the module):

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing_extensions import TypedDict

from langgraph.func import entrypoint


class In(TypedDict):
    a: int


class Out(BaseModel):
    b: str


@entrypoint()
def wf(inputs: In) -> Out:
    return Out(b=str(inputs["a"]))


@entrypoint()
def wf_final(inputs: int, *, previous: Any) -> entrypoint.final[int, str]:
    return entrypoint.final(value=inputs, save=str(inputs))


print(wf.invoke({"a": 1}))  # works
print(wf_final.get_output_jsonschema())  # raises
print(wf.get_input_jsonschema())  # raises
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```
pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: `LangGraphOutput` is not fully defined; you should define `entrypoint`, then call `LangGraphOutput.model_rebuild()`.
```

and for `wf.get_input_jsonschema()`:

```
pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: `LangGraphInput` is not fully defined; you should define `In`, then call `LangGraphInput.model_rebuild()`.
```

### Description

`entrypoint.__call__` gets the input/output types from `inspect.signature(func)` (`libs/langgraph/langgraph/func/__init__.py`). With `from __future__ import annotations` every annotation is a string (`'In'`, `'entrypoint.final[int, str]'`), and the strings are used as-is:

1. They become the channel types, so `get_input_jsonschema()` / `get_output_jsonschema()` raise for any user-defined type.
2. `get_origin('entrypoint.final[int, str]')` is `None`, so `final[R, S]` is never split into return/save types.
3. With `LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK` enabled, `build_serde_allowlist` receives strings, so the user's models aren't allowlisted. On the next run `previous` is deserialized as a plain dict instead of the model.

Removing the future import makes all three work. `StateGraph` already resolves string annotations for nodes and branches via `get_type_hints` (#1835).

Proposed fix: use `inspect.signature(func, eval_str=True)`, and fall back to the current `inspect.signature(func)` if the annotations can't be evaluated (e.g. names imported only under `TYPE_CHECKING`), so nothing that works today breaks. I have the change and regression tests ready, and would like to be assigned to open the PR.

No matching report found for `PersistentDict` serialization-error cleanup on Windows.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

Run on Windows with `langgraph-checkpoint==4.3.1`:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from threading import Lock

from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import PersistentDict

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "checkpoint.pkl"
    store = PersistentDict(filename=str(path))
    store["lock"] = Lock()
    try:
        store.sync()
    except Exception as exc:
        print(type(exc).__name__, exc)
    print("Temporary file remains:", Path(str(path) + ".tmp").exists())
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace

```text
TypeError: cannot pickle '_thread.lock' object

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

PermissionError: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process: '...checkpoint.pkl.tmp'
Temporary file remains: True
```

### Description

`PersistentDict.sync()` attempts to remove the temporary file before closing its handle when `dump()` raises. Windows refuses that deletion, replacing the useful serialization error with `PermissionError` and leaving the partial temporary file. The invalid value should still be rejected; the expected result is the original `TypeError` with the temporary file removed and any previously saved file preserved.

A scoped [patch and regression tests](https://github.com/priy-anshugupta/langgraph/commit/a15c0ba117c4984d0a6f5d1b93b7da616e1a87de) are ready: close the file before attempting cleanup. Two regression cases fail on unchanged main and pass with the patch; they cover new/existing destinations and recovery on a later valid save. A successful-save control also passes. `make format`, `make lint`, and `make test TEST='tests --ignore=tests/test_redis_cache.py'` pass (255 tests); Redis integration tests were excluded. This is Python's local file-handle cleanup, with no serialized-format change or JS runtime counterpart.

Could a maintainer confirm this approach and assign the issue to `priy-anshugupta`? I will open the upstream PR after approval, following the contribution policy.

title: Set of tuples in state is restored as a list from a checkpoint
body:
A state field of type `set[tuple[...]]` comes back from a checkpoint as a `list` of lists, and the node code after a resume then gets a list instead of a set.

Reproduction (`langgraph 1.2.19`, `langgraph-checkpoint 4.3.1`):

```python
from typing import TypedDict

from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from langgraph.types import Command, interrupt


class State(TypedDict):
    visited: set[tuple[int, int]]


def explore(state: State) -> State:
    return {"visited": {(0, 0), (0, 1)}}


def ask(state: State) -> State:
    interrupt("continue?")
    return {}


builder = StateGraph(State)
builder.add_node("explore", explore)
builder.add_node("ask", ask)
builder.add_edge(START, "explore")
builder.add_edge("explore", "ask")
builder.add_edge("ask", END)
graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())

config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
graph.invoke({"visited": set()}, config)

visited = graph.get_state(config).values["visited"]
print(type(visited).__name__, visited)

result = graph.invoke(Command(resume=True), config)
print(type(result["visited"]).__name__, result["visited"])
```

Output:

```
Could not reconstruct builtins.set from checkpoint (TypeError); returning its serialized data instead.
list [[0, 1], [0, 0]]
list [[0, 1], [0, 0]]
```

Expected: `set {(0, 1), (0, 0)}` both times, as for a `set[int]` or a `set[str]`, which round trip correctly.

Cause: `JsonPlusSerializer` encodes a set as a msgpack extension holding its elements. msgpack has no tuple type, so the tuples are decoded as lists, `set([[0, 1], ...])` raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`, and the reconstruction fallback returns the raw list. A list can never have been a set element, so lists inside a decoded `set` or `frozenset` can safely be turned back into tuples. This only affects sets and frozensets, which is the only place a tuple is required for the value to be valid. Tuples elsewhere (for example in a list) still come back as lists, which I am not proposing to change.

I have a fix with tests (about 10 lines in `libs/checkpoint/langgraph/checkpoint/serde/jsonplus.py`) and would like to open a PR if a maintainer approves. It is Python-only, so I don't think the JS side needs a matching change.

The issue text and fix were prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant (Devin CLI) and checked by running the reproduction above on the released packages.

title: feat(langgraph): add Runtime.on_exit for cleanup that runs however a run ends
body:
Adds `Runtime.on_exit(cb)` to register cleanup that runs however the run ends: success, error, cancel, interrupt, or stream closed early. Today "after" hooks don't run on those paths, so resources like QuickJS interpreter slots leak (open-swe#4703 has a workaround). Draft, for discussion.

```python
def node(state, runtime: Runtime):
    slot = open_interpreter()
    runtime.on_exit(slot.close)  # or get_runtime().on_exit(...)
```

There's no new cleanup machinery here. The Pregel loop already has an internal exit stack that unwinds on every exit path, and this just exposes it. Callbacks go onto the root loop's stack, so they run LIFO after every node has stopped and the final checkpoint is saved. Subgraphs register on the root run.

Open questions:
- Should callbacks get the exit reason? QuickJS wants to keep a slot on interrupt and free it on error.
- Should a callback error on a successful run be raised, or only logged?

title: feat(cli): log in to LangSmith without an API key
body:
## Why
`langgraph deploy` and the other control-plane commands required a LangSmith API key. The `langsmith` CLI already supports browser login (OAuth device flow) and stores tokens in `~/.langsmith/config.json`; this lets `langgraph` use the same login.

## What
- New `langgraph_cli/langsmith_auth.py`: reads the active profile (`LANGSMITH_CONFIG_FILE` / `LANGSMITH_PROFILE`), discovers OAuth endpoints (falls back to `<root>/oauth/*`), refreshes the access token, and runs the device-code login with client id `langsmith-cli`.
- `HostBackendClient` accepts an `access_token` callable and sends `Authorization: Bearer …` per request (access tokens live 5 minutes, so it refreshes as needed). `X-Api-Key` is unchanged.
- Credential order: `--api-key` / env / `.env` → profile `api_key` → profile OAuth token. The profile `workspace_id` is used as the tenant when `LANGSMITH_TENANT_ID` is unset.
- New `langgraph login` command. When no credentials exist, an interactive command now starts the login flow instead of prompting for an API key; `--no-input` / `--json` still fail fast, with a message pointing to `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` or `langgraph login`.

The control plane accepts these tokens: `host-backend` auth forwards `Authorization` to the platform `/auth`, which validates LangSmith OAuth JWTs and derives the tenant from the token claims.

## Notes
- JS CLI (langgraphjs) needs a matching change.
- Concurrent refreshes from several processes aren't locked (the Python SDK has a file lock); refresh failures tell the user to run `langgraph login`.
- Not tested end-to-end through a real deploy; the device-code request was smoke-tested against `api.smith.langchain.com`, the rest by unit tests (`tests/unit_tests/test_langsmith_auth.py`).

title: sdk-py: get_client(url=None) accepts timeout= but never applies it — in-process calls cannot be bounded
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangGraph rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Related Issues / PRs

- #6654 — `runs.stream` with `url=None` buffering or hanging in v0.6 (closed). Same transport,
  different symptom: that report is about streaming updates arriving late, this one is about
  `timeout=` never being applied. Not a duplicate.
- #9499 — same class of failure on the network path (server heartbeats reset the read timeout).
  Separate symptom and separate layer, so a separate issue.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

Installing a LangGraph server locally to reproduce is heavy, so this supplies the loopback
transport directly, with a handler that sleeps 10 s. `langgraph-sdk` and `httpx` only:

```python
import asyncio, time
import httpx

async def slow_app(scope, receive, send):
    if scope["type"] != "http":
        return
    await asyncio.sleep(10)                     # a handler that outlives any client budget
    await send({"type": "http.response.start", "status": 200,
                "headers": [(b"content-type", b"application/json")]})
    await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": b'{"thread_id": "x"}'})

async def main():
    import langgraph_sdk._async.client as lgclient
    # url=None builds its transport from this factory; substitute one that serves slow_app
    lgclient.get_asgi_transport = lambda *a, **kw: (
        lambda app=None, root_path="": httpx.ASGITransport(app=slow_app)
    )
    client = lgclient.get_client(url=None, timeout=1.0)
    print(client.http.client.timeout)           # Timeout(timeout=1.0)
    t = time.perf_counter()
    await client.threads.get("x")               # no exception, no bound
    print(f"returned after {time.perf_counter() - t:.1f}s")

asyncio.run(main())
```

When a LangGraph server package is installed, the factory supplies its own transport instead of this
one; the measurement quoted below uses that transport, unmodified.

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```
client timeout = Timeout(timeout=1.0)
returned after 10.1s        # the handler's whole duration; timeout=1.0 was never applied
```

Python 3.11.16, `langgraph-sdk` 0.4.10, `httpx` 0.28.1, in a clean environment with only the SDK
installed.

Same result through the transport the SDK actually builds when a LangGraph server package is
installed, driven by a handler that sleeps 10 s: before any fix, `get_client(url=None, timeout=1.0)`
returned after 10.00 s with no exception.

### Description

* I am using `get_client(url=None)` from inside a node and passing `timeout=` to bound a slow or
  stuck handler. The docstring describes `url=None` as attempting an in-process connection first.
* I expect the call to raise `ReadTimeout` after the configured interval, the way it does against
  a URL.
* Instead the argument is accepted but never applied: the caller waits for the handler however long
  it takes. Replace the 10 s sleep with a handler that never returns and the call never returns
  either.

The same setting against `url="http://..."`, pointed at a server that accepts the connection and never
answers, does what it should: `httpx.ReadTimeout` after 1.02 s. So `timeout=1.0` is honoured on the
network path and dropped on the loopback path.

Note that `get_sync_client(url=None)` always goes over TCP, so this affects the async factory only.

This is the path used inside a node, which is exactly where a stuck handler parks a request slot,
so the missing bound is what turns one slow call into a hung worker.

Wrapping the call in `asyncio.timeout(...)` works as a workaround, but `timeout=` being accepted
and silently ignored is the bug.

Requesting assignment so I can open the PR. I have the patch and tests ready; the change applies
the client's existing timeout to the loopback path rather than adding a new option, and
`timeout=None` keeps meaning "wait indefinitely".

title: sdk-py: timeout= does not bound runs.stream() — server SSE heartbeats reset the read timeout forever
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangGraph rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Related Issues / PRs

- #9299 — comment-only SSE heartbeats, same traffic, different symptom (phantom event after an
  event ID). Not a duplicate: it is about decoding, this is about the call never returning.
- #6654 — in-process streaming behaviour in v0.6 (closed). Background, not a duplicate.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

A local socket server that answers `text/event-stream` and then writes the same comment-only
heartbeat the server writes, every second, and nothing else. Standard library plus
`langgraph-sdk` only.

```python
import socket, threading, time
from langgraph_sdk import get_sync_client

s = socket.socket()
s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
s.listen(1)
PORT = s.getsockname()[1]

def serve():
    conn, _ = s.accept()
    conn.recv(65536)                                   # request line + headers, ignored
    conn.sendall(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n"
                 b"Content-Type: text/event-stream\r\n"
                 b"Cache-Control: no-cache\r\n\r\n")
    while True:
        conn.sendall(b": heartbeat\n\n")               # bytes, never an event
        time.sleep(1)

threading.Thread(target=serve, daemon=True).start()
time.sleep(0.1)

client = get_sync_client(url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}", api_key=None, timeout=10)
print(client.http.client.timeout)          # Timeout(timeout=10.0)
for part in client.runs.stream(thread_id="t", assistant_id="a", input={}):
    print(part)                            # never reached; the loop never ends
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

None. That is the report.

```
client timeout                        server                         outcome
Timeout(connect=5, read=300, ...)     accepts, then stays silent     ReadTimeout after 300 s   (control)
Timeout(connect=5, read=300, ...)     heartbeats, no event            did not return; my watchdog killed the process at 962 s; no exception
Timeout(timeout=10.0)                 heartbeats, no event            did not return; my watchdog killed the process at 181 s; no exception
Timeout(timeout=5)                    real `langgraph dev` server     one metadata event at 0.7 s, then nothing; killed at 60 s; no exception
```

The timeout is not missing, and it is not the default that is wrong: on a server that accepts the
connection and says nothing, the same client raises `ReadTimeout` on schedule. It is only inert
when the connection carries heartbeats.

The last row is the same client against a real `langgraph dev` server running a graph whose node
sleeps. This one is a legitimately long node, which is the point: from the client, a long node and a
stuck one look identical, so the caller needs a way to set its own ceiling. In every run with
heartbeats the process had to be killed; the client never returned or raised on its own.

### Description

* I am calling `client.runs.stream(...)` against a LangGraph server and passing `timeout=`,
  expecting a bound on how long the call can go without progress.
* I expect the call to raise `ReadTimeout` when nothing arrives for the configured interval.
* Instead the call runs forever, because the server keeps the connection alive with SSE comment
  lines.

The heartbeats are intentional — I assume to keep long runs from being cut by proxies — and I am not
asking to change them. The problem is that `timeout=` then has no effect on a stream at all.

The reason is what the read timeout measures. `read` is the maximum gap between two *bytes*.
While a stream is open the server writes a comment-only SSE heartbeat, `: heartbeat`, every few
seconds — a 20-second `curl -N` capture against a local server shows three of them. A comment is
bytes, so every heartbeat resets the clock, and no interval a caller can pass will ever elapse.
Against a stream that never finishes, `timeout=` is silently inert.

Both the sync and async clients decode the stream the same way; the repro above uses the sync one.

One consequence: a run that never finishes (a stuck node, a graph waiting on something that never
arrives, a run the server lost track of) parks the caller forever. Async callers can wrap the call in
`asyncio.timeout(...)`; sync callers have no equivalent, because a thread blocked in a socket read
cannot be interrupted.

This is a design question as much as a bug. **Which layer should carry the bound?** A client-side
opt-in (a "no decoded event for N seconds" deadline, default off, existing behaviour untouched) is
one option; a server-side limit on stream lifetime or idle time is another, and it would also cover
clients that are not the Python SDK. I am aware `AGENTS.md` says the SDKs stay thin and that new
public surface for ergonomics alone is ruled out, so I do not want to assume the client-side answer
is the one you want. I have prepared a client-side opt-in, but I would rather ask which layer you
want before opening anything.

### System Info

```
System Information
------------------
> OS:  Windows
> OS Version:  10.0.22631
> Python Version:  3.11.16 (main, Sep  1 2026, 14:15:24) [MSC v.1944 64 bit (AMD64)]

Package Information
-------------------
> langchain_core: 1.7.1
> langsmith: 0.14.15
> langgraph_sdk: 0.4.10

Other Dependencies
------------------
> anyio: 4.15.1
> httpx: 0.28.1
> orjson: 3.13.0
> pydantic: 2.14.2
```

The last row of the table was measured against `langgraph dev` with langgraph-api 0.17.0 on this
machine.

If the client is the right layer for this, I have an opt-in patch and tests ready (no breaking
change, default keeps today's behaviour) and will open a PR once the issue is assigned.

title: update_state on the head of a failed run drops a finished sibling's writes
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure this is a bug in LangGraph rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version.
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example.

### Description

`update_state()` on the head checkpoint of a failed (or interrupted) run drops the durable output of already-finished parallel siblings.

Graph: `START -> a`, `START -> b`, both `-> c`. In one superstep `a` succeeds (`a` appends `"a"` to `log`) and `b` raises. `invoke()` propagates the error; `get_state()` still shows `values={'log': ['a']}`, `next=('b',)`. The user recovers with:

```python
graph.update_state(cfg, {"fixed": True, "log": ["manual"]}, as_node="b")
graph.invoke(None, cfg)
```

Expected: `a`'s finished write stays in the state (as it does on a plain retry resume), i.e. `log` ends around `['a', 'manual', 'c']`.

Actual: the head checkpoint is rebuilt from the saved checkpoint's *committed* values only, and `c` runs with `{'log': ['manual'], 'fixed': True}`, final `{'log': ['manual', 'c']}`. `a` is not re-run (`runs={'a': 1, ...}`), so its stored pending write is silently lost with no error.

Comparison reproduced with `InMemorySaver` and `SqliteSaver`, sync and async, and with `interrupt()` instead of a raised exception:

```
[mem-update]  after failure: next=('b',) values={'log': ['a']} runs={'a': 1, 'b': 1}
[mem-update]  recovered via update_state: final={'log': ['manual', 'c'], 'fixed': True} runs={'a': 1, 'b': 1, 'c': 1}
[mem-resume]  recovered via resume:       final={'log': ['a', 'b', 'c']}            runs={'a': 1, 'b': 2, 'c': 1}
[sqlite-update] recovered via update_state: final={'log': ['manual', 'c'], 'fixed': True}
```

Code pointers: `libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/main.py:1673` builds the checkpoint from `saved.checkpoint` committed values only; `main.py:2055` (`_store_or_fork_delta_writes`) preserves only delta-channel pending writes; `main.py:2068` passes only the update's tasks to `apply_writes`. A normal resume replays loaded pending writes into tasks instead (`pregel/_loop.py:708-730`).

### Reproduction

```python
# see the script: two parallel nodes, one raises, recover via update_state(as_node=...) then invoke(None)
```

Self-contained script (`final_error_sibling.py`, plus an interrupt variant `sibling_writes_final.py`, an async variant, and a pending-task variant) is available; happy to attach it. No services or API keys.

### Expected behavior

When the addressed checkpoint is the head of the failed run (not a historical fork), recovering via `update_state` should keep the finished siblings' pending writes, matching a plain retry resume.

### Additional context

- Why this is not just fork semantics: merged #6389 deliberately avoids replaying pending writes on **historical** checkpoints (to prevent stale data), but here the update checkpoint *is* the next child of the head and the sibling's write is durable. Delta channels already get fork/head machinery (`_store_or_fork_delta_writes`, `checkpoint_superseded`); plain channels get nothing.
- Suggested direction: when the addressed checkpoint is not superseded, apply the finished tasks' output writes from `saved.pending_writes` alongside the update (mirroring `_reapplies_pending_writes`); keep the current behavior for historical forks.
- Related but distinct: #9076 (open; `update_state` clears `StateSnapshot.interrupts`), #8653 (closed, config-injected checkpointer), #6389 (merged; stale-fork replay rationale).
- Searched open and closed issues/PRs for `update_state` × pending writes / parallel siblings / error recovery: no duplicate.
